prompts:
Use case: compositing.
Asset type: ONE integrated transparent isometric game sprite: a ruined monster deployment station.
Input image 1: the purple floor pad, base design reference.
Input image 2: the heavily damaged armor rack, equipment and damage reference.
Primary request: redesign and combine both into ONE BEAUTIFUL COHERENT structure. The previous version looked like two unrelated stickers, a tiny tall rack sitting on a very bright badge. This should look intentionally built as one compact dungeon fixture, with unified perspective, materials, scale, lighting and contact shadows.
Design:
- Keep a square low stone plinth with a true 2:1 diamond top footprint, shallow stone lip, aged brass corner caps and rim.
- Replace the large bright cartoon skull-and-feet badge with a subdued inset of deep dusty amethyst stone. Retain just TWO SMALL elegant ivory foot-position inlays near the FRONT center as the clear placement cue. No second skull emblem on the floor: the single skull on the rack is the focal point.
- The broken wooden T-rack rises directly from a BRASS SOCKET BOLTED INTO THE BACK-CENTER of the plinth. REMOVE the rack's separate splayed wooden feet entirely. There must be a believable built-in connection to the plinth, no floating or double platform.
- A compact cracked ivory skull helmet crowns the rack. Make its missing quarter-dome and dark hollow readable, but reduce the skull size slightly to fit a pleasing balanced silhouette.
- Keep the large damaged shoulder armor, one pauldron hanging by a purple strap on the left, the other chipped on the right; fractured wood crossbar and ragged purple fabric. Drape one cloth strip naturally toward the base and unify its muted purple with the inset.
- A broken small shield leans naturally against the RIGHT BACK edge of the plinth, touching both rack and platform. Keep the split plank and missing rim wedge.
- Keep the front third of the purple top EMPTY and visibly walkable, showing the small paired foot-position inlays. All equipment stays WITHIN the platform footprint when projected, no debris beyond it.
Art direction: polished hand-painted 3D fantasy dungeon game asset, cute chunky proportions but tasteful and not toy-like. Aged desaturated brass rather than bright yellow gold, dusty violet rather than neon purple, warm ivory and deep walnut. Soft warm upper-left light with consistent tight contact shadows painted ON the structure. Clear hierarchy: skull and broken armor above, subtle foundation below. Broad shapes readable when entire fixture is 120 pixels wide.
Camera and technical composition:
- Orthographic 2:1 isometric ground plane; the platform diamond top is EXACTLY twice as wide as deep on screen, matching input 1.
- Entire visible sprite should be slightly wider than tall, roughly width:height 1.12:1; keep rack COMPACT, not towering. Platform occupies the full width, rack/armor spans only the middle 55 percent of that width.
- One centered complete integrated object, at least 8 percent transparent padding on all sides; no parts cut off. The base's left/right points and front tip must be plainly defined for game alignment.
- Genuine transparent alpha background. NO background, external ground shadow, border, text, digits, watermarks, extra characters, living skeleton or assembled soldier.
Do not merely paste the references together: repaint a cohesive integrated fixture, preserving the recognizable broken equipment but improving overall visual balance.

Use case: background-extraction.
Edit ONLY the background/transparency of this integrated monster deployment station. Preserve the actual entire plinth, foot-position inlays, rack, socket, torn cloth, armor, skull and shield EXACTLY as drawn, same geometry, same colors, same camera, same scale and positions.
Remove ALL the blurry brown/purple glowing haze and drop-shadow halo surrounding the object. Every pixel outside the hard silhouette of the physical object must be fully transparent alpha 0. This includes negative spaces around hanging armor and through cloth tears. Keep natural antialiased edge pixels on the object itself. Shadows painted on the physical plinth and the objects remain.
No external shadow, no fog, no glow, no gradient, no black or checkerboard background. Do not add anything. Do not repaint or resize the object. Output one clean transparent PNG game sprite with generous transparent padding.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit this integrated monster deployment station into its matching CLEAR OCCUPIED BASE TILE.
Remove the entire upright wooden rack, skull helmet, both pieces of shoulder armor, hanging straps, all cloth, leaning broken shield, and the brass post socket. Reconstruct the exposed purple stone top naturally.
Keep the base platform EXACTLY: same diamond outline, same footprint perspective, same low stone thickness, same brass corner caps and rim, same muted purple inset, same small paired ivory foot-position marks at the front, same lighting and wear, same size and location on the canvas. Leave its middle and back clear so a skeleton guard can stand there. No skull symbol or new ornament on the floor.
Output the single base tile only on genuinely transparent alpha. Everything outside the physical base outline must be fully transparent. No environment glow, no shadow halo, no backdrop, no extra objects, no text, no watermark. Preserve the platform geometry precisely for switching between two game states.
